text:
sania: quick q — when the automatic fallback triggers and we hand off to the cheaper model, do we want 100% audit traces for a short window or just sampled traces? thinking about storage and privacy.
mike: my gut says sample by default (1-5%) and escalate to full traces for anomalies. otherwise logs explode. :exploding_head:
elaine: agree on sampling. but operator UX needs a way to 'force-capture' for a customer or a specific request id. can we add a button in the Console that marks a request for full retention?
jordan: +1. also we need to be careful about PII — any forced-capture must trigger a redact step and tag the trace for restricted access.
sam: product perspective: customers will ask for auditability of rollouts. if we sample, surface sampling ratios clearly and provide a link to the sampled request set for a given rollout window.
ops-bot: Note: recent prod incident increased fallback rate x4 for 15m — might be a good defrag window to test retention policy (incident #2021-03-fb)
mike: rough config proposal:
```
fallback.audit:
  sample_rate: 0.02 # default
  anomaly_full_capture: true
  anomaly_threshold: 0.05 # fallback spike relative to baseline
  force_capture_label: "capture-for-cs"
```
sania: that looks reasonable. how do we surface the anomaly_full_capture behavior in the Console? we don't want surprise costs.
elaine: show an inline banner when an auto-full-capture is about to kick in: "Fallback volume crossed 5% above baseline — capturing full traces for 10m." with an opt-out toggle per-org.
jordan: and add per-model quotas for capture bytes so a single noisy customer can't blow through retention budgets.
mike: technical note — KV caching/metadata should let us toggle capture at router time; we can tag requests with `capture=true` and a downstream ingestion job will route to the high-retention path.
sam: for rollout UX: add a small sampling-meter on the rollout card that shows expected storage delta and an estimate of additional cost if full-capture triggers. transparency > surprises.
elaine: audit trail requirement: every automatic switch (sample->full) must be logged as an event in the rollout timeline with link to the trigger metric and relevant traces.
sania: ok next: what about debug mode for canaries? maybe 100% capture for canary percentage (e.g., first 0-1% of traffic) for N minutes.
jordan: yes, canary should be full by default for first X minutes or Y requests. then drop to sampled.
mike: implementable. we'll add config keys: `canary.full_capture_duration_mins` and `canary.max_full_capture_requests`.
sam: can we also let customers request a retrospective increase in sampling window for an incident? like retro-raise to pull more samples from archived stats? should flag legal/privacy constraints though.
elaine: retrospective expansion is tricky — we typically only keep sampled payloads. we can expand metadata indexes but not payload content unless archived. recommend an epidemiology-style approach: keep metadata long-term, payload short-term.
sania: cool. next action items:
- mike: spin up a PR with the config schema and router tagging API
- elaine: mockup Console banners and rollout card sampling meter
- jordan: propose quota limits and redact pipeline notes
- sam: write customer-facing FAQ/opt-in language for audit capture
mike: i'll drop a draft config PR by EOD and ping @sania for review.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary deploy for rollout-capture-proto in staging at 2024-06-18T22:00Z
sania: thanks — let's review in the design huddle tomorrow. :thumbsup:
